mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive monthly observations
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of at least 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by ≥0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month periods of sustained UNRATE increases ≥0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad-based weakness in demand drivers, which amplifies recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% combined with a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three-month stretches where PAYEMS exceeds 100,000 monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE change within ±0.1pp) signals improving consumer demand without overheating labor markets, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 1% AND |UNRATE monthly change| ≤ 0.1pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises >1% month-over-month and UNRATE changes by ≤0.1pp.
